title: P20 follow-up: shorten five-layer Muon warmup to 100 steps
description: P20 in the opposite direction to 022: shorten only pretraining warmup from 200 to 100 steps on five-layer incumbent 051-claude, retaining peak rates and the absolute-wall-clock cosine schedule. Earlier full-strength Muon and auxiliary AdamW updates may learn features that transfer better through the fixed downstream expert-iteration procedure.
hypothesis: Five-layer training gets about 2340 updates in the fixed 300 seconds, so 200-step warmup spends a larger fraction of training at reduced rates than the old four-layer model. Halving warmup may improve early feature acquisition and the starting policy for expert iteration without raising peak rates. Earlier 600-step warmup failed on the old AdamW baseline (022); this is a new direction and optimizer/depth regime, not a repeat. Expect round-1 sample accuracy to improve on at least two seeds relative to 051 values 0.0630/0.0494/0.0749. Larger integrated LR-scaled decay also accompanies the schedule change, so any gain cannot isolate early feature acquisition as its cause.
expected_delta: Central prediction +3 to +15 dev-transfer solves at true length >=7 relative to exact incumbent mean 286.333333 (288/260/311); plausible downside -40 from early instability. Expect about 2300-2400 pretraining updates and no direct kernel or inference overhead; learned generation lengths may change total runtime. At about 7.8 steps/s, warmup ends near 13 seconds rather than 26 seconds plus setup time. Keep/discard uses only the fixed downstream mean on seeds 0,1,2; lower pretraining loss alone is insufficient.

arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) are in Muon. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters throughout; hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction, including the former finish window; integrated decay can differ with throughput.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.schedule_detail: Steps 1..99: AdamW LR=0.001*step/100 and Muon LR=0.01*step/100. At step>=100 both use the unchanged cosine of elapsed absolute wall time / 300 seconds, with floor fraction 0.1; no cosine-time restart or duration change.

config.init: Fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter after moving to device. Gain = 0.02 * sqrt(max(rows, columns)); exact element second moment 0.0004. All 20 hidden matrices: qkv (768,256), proj (256,256), fc1 (1024,256), fc2 (256,1024) in each of five blocks. QKV initialized jointly. Embedding and readout keep the fork's normal(0.02) draws; biases zero; LayerNorm weight 1 and bias 0. No reinitialization during RL. The fifth block consumes extra global-RNG draws during construction, so random initial weights are not bitwise identical to 043's for a given seed; the init rule is identical.
